text:
Ava: heads-up — customer 'AcroHealth' on Dedicated is seeing sporadic 401s from their private gateway. They say it started after we flipped the new istio-authz filter on their VPC LB.
Dmitri: can you paste a sample request/resp or a log line? sounds like header forwarding issue again.
Ava: sample from our gateway logs (tail):
```
2026-01-28T12:03:41Z INFO inbound request path=/api/v1/generate method=POST src=10.12.5.34 headers={Host: rdw-acro.private, Authorization: "Bearer <redacted>"} upstream=/svc/inference status=200
2026-01-28T12:04:02Z INFO lb-probe path=/_hc src=10.8.0.1 headers={Host: rdw-acro.private} upstream=/svc/inference status=401
```
Notice the probe to /_hc lacks Authorization and triggers authz, then our fallback kicks in and the session gets rejected for a short window. customer sees intermittent 401s when LB healthcheck races with real requests.
Priya: which LB/probe type? GCP NLB? AWS NLB? classic LB? behaviour differs.
Ava: customer is on GCP, using TCP NLB with HTTP healthcheck hitting /_hc. The NLB healthcheck IPs are in a small pool, and it looks like the probe sometimes reuses connection where headers are omitted.
Dmitri: that rings a bell — TCP NLB healthchecks can reset headers depending on proxy mode. Istio envoy ext_authz policy by default checks Authorization header and denies if missing. We recently tightened the policy to "require jwt OR allow-healthcheck" but /_hc wasn't included in the allow list.
Eli: quick repro from my laptop (using curl) against the customer's edge (ip masked):
```
# good: direct request with auth
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer TOK" -X POST https://10.11.12.13/api/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# probe: healthcheck connection (no header added)
curl -i -X GET https://10.11.12.13/_hc
```
Response: 401 on /_hc when authz filter requires Authorization; sometimes the probe arrives between the LB connection reuse and a real request.
Priya: can we check envoy logs to confirm header drop/connection reuse? Also need to confirm istio filter skipPaths.
Ava: envoy trace from the edge node: 
```
[2026-01-28T12:04:02Z] envoy access_log: path=/_hc, downstream_remote=10.8.0.1, x-forwarded-for=10.8.0.1, authorization="-"
```
So Authorization header is literally missing.
Dmitri: known pattern: GCP TCP NLB health probe opens a connection, sends minimal bytes, and if backend uses keepalive the next request on that connection may not include application-layer headers the way our proxy expects. With HTTP(S) health checks the LB may rewrite or strip headers too. We should treat healthcheck paths as unauthenticated or require the LB to send a specific header.
Eli: quick fix options:
- Add /_hc to istio ext_authz allowedPaths list (temporary)
- Configure LB healthcheck to use a path that we treat as unauthenticated and return 200 with simple handler
- Make the authz filter tolerant: if request source IP in healthcheck range, bypass auth check
- Have LB inject a header (X-Health-Check: yes) and whitelist that header in authz
Priya: which is least risky for Dedicated/private customers? security team may push back on making authz looser.
Dmitri: whitelist by source IP + path is safest short-term. We can also adjust the healthcheck to use a unique path (/_hc-internal) that returns 200 and is unauthenticated — that requires customer LB config change.
Ava: I tried a quick patch on a canary (istio ext_authz config) to allow /_hc and healthcheck CIDR; it removed the 401s for that customer. But we need org-level approval before rolling to all Dedicated clusters.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2345 created (severity: P2) — 10 affected customers reported 401 spikes. Assigned to: eng-infra, security.
Priya: steps to reproduce for the ticket (copyable):
1) Deploy a service behind edge-proxy with ext_authz enforcing Authorization header
2) Configure GCP TCP NLB health check hitting /_hc (HTTP GET) with keepalive enabled
3) Rapidly fire authenticated POSTs and observe 401s correlating with healthcheck times
4) Collect envoy/access logs and the LB healthcheck source IPs
Example curl repro attached above.
Dmitri: config snippet we used for the temporary allow-list (istio ext_authz):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  allowed_paths: 
    - "/_hc"
  allowed_source_cidrs:
    - "35.191.0.0/16"  # example GCP healthcheck range
```
Eli: longer-term fixes we should discuss:
- make ext_authz aware of connection reuse & not treat missing header on probe paths as malicious
- require LB to include a signed header for healthchecks (X-Redwood-HC: <sig>) that ext_authz can validate
- update our deployment docs for Dedicated/Private to call out healthcheck path + CIDR requirements
Ava: customer asked for an ETA for a proper fix. Can we do a safe config change (allow CIDR + path) and then schedule a hardened change in 2 weeks?
Dmitri: yes — propose a phased approach: immediate per-customer canary, then global rollout after security review. I'll prepare the PR and tag @Priya for the security exception review.
Priya: will review, but prefer CIDR+path over turning off auth for paths. Also want an audit log entry whenever we bypass auth for health checks.
sre-bot: deploy job queued: canary/allow-hc-acrohealth by Dmitri (job id: deploy-8923)
deploy-bot: deploy-8923 started on cluster-dedicated-12 (canary)
Ava: deploy shows green on canary. Customer reports 200s again. I'll keep monitoring and ask them to confirm no further 401s.
Eli: followups for the ticket INC-2345:
- engineering to submit PR with parametric allow-list and audit logging (owner: Dmitri)
- security to sign off on CIDR ranges + audit (owner: Priya)
- support to notify customers & provide repro steps + mitigation doc (owner: Ava)
- infra to add note in Dedicated quickstart about LB healthcheck config (owner: Eli)
Ava: cc @Priya @Dmitri @Eli — assigning to ops board. Customer thanked us for fast response.
Priya: leaving a snippet for ops runbook: when customers see intermittent 401s after LB changes, check: healthcheck path, LB type (TCP vs HTTP), healthcheck IP ranges, envoy access logs for missing Authorization header, and whether connection reuse is enabled on the LB.
Dmitri: adding a short-term automation: if we detect 5 401s within 30s and source IP matches known healthcheck CIDRs, mark as "probable healthcheck strip" and auto-create incident with suggested remediation.
Ava: closing the loop — will update INC-2345 with customer confirmation and link to PR when available. :thumbsup:
